clue.text: Mansion of rock sited in Memphis to look good in countryside

definitions.text: Mansion of rock sited in Memphis

parts.note: to grace something is to make it look good, to adorn it
land is open country, as in working the land

explanation.surface: A rural setting is said to show off a famous Memphis house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here, not a container signal: the two pieces sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley, the king of rock and roll, lived at this Memphis estate, now a museum.

clue.text: Problem about the Queen and something in the royal blood

indicators.note: the sum goes around, encircling the royal abbreviation placed within it

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem set at school
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A difficulty concerning the monarch and her blue blood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royal' merely echoes the Queen in the surface; the liquid part of anyone's blood is what is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: The clear fluid left when blood clots is a component of blood, royal or otherwise.

clue.text: Tattoos big belly making dark marking

parts.note: to ink someone is to tattoo them, so tattoos means inks
a pot or pot belly is a large paunch

explanation.surface: A tattooed paunch leaves a dark mark on its owner.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot of spilt writing fluid is a dark stain on paper.

clue.text: Small clothes club banned will make one drool

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the club letter is barred from the word for clothes, so it is removed

parts.note: clobber is British slang for clothes or gear
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: Banning a club for its small kit will make someone drool with envy.
explanation.walkthrough: CLOBBER is everyday British slang for clothes; 'will make one' is a link joining wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To slaver or let saliva run from the mouth is to drool.

clue.text: Artist is gloomier losing something Giotto famously drew

indicators.note: losing tells us to drop a letter from the word for gloomier

parts.note: dour means stern and gloomy, so gloomier gives dourer
Giotto reputedly drew a perfect freehand circle for the Pope, so a circle: the letter O

explanation.surface: A painter is said to be more morose after losing one of Giotto's drawings.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend of Giotto's O: asked for a sample of his work, he drew a perfect circle freehand.
explanation.definitionFit: Albrecht Durer was the great German Renaissance painter and engraver.

clue.text: Trapped inside plane's tail I would become good and restless

indicators.note: the pieces that follow are held within the tail-fin word

parts.note: the fin is the vertical tail surface of an aircraft
I'd is the contraction of I would
to get is to become, as in get angry

explanation.surface: A stowaway in a plane's tail hopes to turn good and grows uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plane's tail' is not the last letter of plane but the tail part of an aircraft, its FIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who keeps squirming and cannot sit still is restless.

clue.text: Travel in white van

indicators.note: the travel word is set inside the word for white

parts.note: wan means pale or white-faced
to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone is moving about in a white van.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon is a vehicle for carrying goods, as is a van; in railways a goods wagon is also called a van.

clue.text: Cut back boring work of testers

indicators.note: back tells us to read the word for cut in reverse

parts.note: to axe is to cut, as in axing jobs
mining is work done by boring into the ground

explanation.surface: Cutbacks in tunnelling work for quality inspectors.
explanation.definitionFit: An examining board is one belonging to testers, so the word works adjectivally for them.

clue.text: Like repayment from PCs, etc, mostly loud with rubbish cladding

indicators.note: the rubbish word covers or encases the other pieces like cladding on a building

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbishy goods
PCs and the like fall under IT, information technology

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word for loud

parts.note: forte is the musical term for loud

explanation.surface: Computers and loud junk are offered in some sort of payback deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Retaliation in kind, giving back what one received, is a form of repayment.

clue.text: Force in iron structure for support

indicators.note: the force word goes inside the symbol for iron

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
to ram is to force, as in ram home

explanation.surface: Applying force to an iron girder for support.
explanation.definitionFit: A framework or skeleton is a structure that holds something up.

clue.text: English flower, for example, grand as a seasonal gift

parts.note: the aster is a daisy-like garden flower
eg, exempli gratia, means for example
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: An English bloom, for instance, makes a grand present at the right time of year.
explanation.definitionFit: A chocolate egg is the traditional present given at the spring festival.

clue.text: As this is apart at the foot

indicators.note: the clue says As plus this entry is a word for apart, so taking As away leaves the entry

parts.note: asunder means apart, into pieces
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cryptic riddle: something which, after As, means apart, also means at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a riddle: the first word joined to this entry spells a word meaning apart, so the surface sense of 'As' is a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Underneath or beneath means at the foot of something.

clue.text: Admission of policeman taking ecstasy to collapse violently

parts.note: a policeman admitting his job says I'm Plod; Plod is British slang for a police officer, from Mr Plod in the Noddy books
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A police officer confesses to taking drugs and falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: PLOD is British slang for the police, after the constable in children's Noddy stories.
explanation.definitionFit: To burst inwards and cave in is to collapse violently.

clue.text: Book transport for a number of passengers

definitions.meaning: a volume containing several works collected together

definitions.text: transport for a number of passengers
definitions.meaning: the old full name for a bus, a vehicle carrying many people

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a collected volume of works and the original name of a public bus.

clue.text: Mayan carving guessed likely Yucatec — perhaps Honduran in origins

indicators.note: the origins of the words are their first letters, which are picked out

explanation.surface: Someone guesses an ancient Mayan inscription probably came from Yucatan, or perhaps Honduras.
explanation.definitionFit: A carved symbol or character, such as those in Mayan script, is a glyph.

clue.text: Will last word on trial end in judgement?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the last word follows the trial word

parts.note: a test is a trial
amen is said as the final word of a prayer

indicators.note: end in picks out the final letter of judgement

explanation.surface: Is a will the final word in a court case at the point of judgement?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a will is not really the last word on a trial; the surface is a courtroom picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document disposing of one's estate.

clue.text: Group of workers reportedly equipped for life under water

indicators.note: reportedly tells us the word is heard, so we want something that sounds the same

parts.note: a fish is gilled, equipped with gills to breathe in water

explanation.surface: Workers said to be fitted out for an underwater existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval association of craftsmen or merchants was a trade body.

clue.text: Cotton magnate joining ship and plane pioneer

parts.note: Noah's ark was a ship
the Wright brothers flew the first powered aeroplane

explanation.surface: A textile tycoon teams up with a ship and an aviation pioneer.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Arkwright invented the water frame and built early cotton mills in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Arkwright made a fortune from mechanised cotton spinning in the industrial revolution.

clue.text: Mental power and time to take in new language

parts.note: ESP is extrasensory perception, a supposed mental power
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Psychic power and time are needed to learn a fresh language.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'to' of the clue is fodder, not a link: TO takes in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Zamenhof's invented tongue is meant as an international auxiliary language.

clue.text: Team left contest about law limiting who can succeed

indicators.note: about signals that the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A side walks out of a match over a rule on who can take part next.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1701 Act of Settlement fixes the line of succession to the British throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1701 statute barred Catholics and fixed the Protestant line of succession to the throne.

clue.text: Duo against Dave's reforms as not being helpful

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are shaped anew into a different arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the s counting as a letter

explanation.surface: A pair oppose Dave's changes as being unhelpful.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that puts one at a disadvantage is unfavourable, not helping.

clue.text: Cure for what cigarette addict often has

definitions.meaning: to preserve fish or meat by exposing it to wood fumes
a puff on a cigarette, a cigarette break

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both preserving food with fumes and the cigarette a smoker frequently takes.

clue.text: Religious leader's short talk

indicators.note: short means the word for talk is cut off before its last letter

parts.note: rabbit is British slang for chatter, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork, talk

explanation.surface: A clergyman's brief speech.
explanation.walkthrough: To rabbit (on) is British slang for to talk at length, from rhyming slang rabbit and pork = talk.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish religious teacher and leader of a congregation is a rabbi.

clue.text: Lender's right to silence over identical notes under way of working

definitions.note: read as Lender is, the 's being is

indicators.note: in a down clue the rest is placed under the working-method letters, so they come first

parts.note: MO is modus operandi, a way of working
to gag someone is to silence them
E and E are two identical musical notes

explanation.surface: A lender's right to silence is set against routine procedure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is only a link in this down clue, and 'Lender's' reads as 'Lender is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In a home loan the bank or building society that lends the money holds the charge on the property.

clue.text: Scornful humour displayed by male band

parts.note: wit is clever humour
he is the male pronoun
a ring is a band, as a wedding band

explanation.surface: A man in a group shows contemptuous humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A withering look or remark is one full of scorn, meant to shrivel its target.

clue.text: Infection from smoke duct in pub, an unknown first in Africa

indicators.note: the duct is placed inside the word for pub

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a flue carries smoke up a chimney
Z is one of the letters used for unknown quantities in algebra

indicators.note: first in picks the opening letter of Africa

explanation.surface: Picking up a bug from a pub chimney, an unexplained first in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The flu is a contagious viral infection of the respiratory system.

clue.text: Not heard of sin — Laud Bible never started?

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its start, its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An unknown sin of Archbishop Laud: a Bible that was never begun?
explanation.walkthrough: Laud was a 17th-century Archbishop of Canterbury; the surface invents a Bible of his.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too quiet to be picked up by the ear is not heard.

clue.text: Feeble agent getting in little work

indicators.note: the small-work piece gets inside the word for agent

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A weak secret agent gets a small job.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppy means weak and sentimental, lacking backbone.

clue.text: Biblical patriarch, an individual that's set up church

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: one is a single individual

explanation.surface: A patriarch from the Bible, a man who founded a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Enoch, father of Methuselah, is one of the antediluvian patriarchs in Genesis.

clue.text: Son in row over repeated test

indicators.note: the son letter is placed inside the other piece
over tells us the word for row is turned back to front

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A son quarrels over having to take another exam.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after failing it the first time.
